payload.translation: To hold and fill it is not as good as to let it be; to measure and sharpen it is not to be able to sustain it; gold and jade fill the hall, yet no one can guard them; wealth and fame are attained, yet pride is lost, and one's own blame is given; success in achievement and attainment, yet one retires from the world. issues.span: wealth and fame are attained, yet pride is lost, and one's own blame is given
issues.advice: The source 富貴而驕自遺其咎 means 'to be wealthy and honored yet arrogant is to bring calamity upon oneself.' The translation inverts the logic: pride is not 'lost' but is the cause, and 自遺其咎 means 'to leave oneself a fault/calamity,' not 'one's own blame is given.' Render as 'wealth and honor accompanied by arrogance bring calamity upon oneself.'

issues.span: to measure and sharpen it is not to be able to sustain it
issues.advice: 揣而銳之不可長保 means 'what is hammered/sharpened to a point cannot be preserved for long.' 'To measure' misreads 揣 (to pound/hammer), and 'is not to be able to sustain it' is awkward and loses 長保 ('long preserved').

issues.span: success in achievement and attainment, yet one retires from the world
issues.advice: 功成名遂身退 means 'when the work is done and fame achieved, to withdraw the self' — 身退 is withdrawing oneself, not 'retiring from the world' (which suggests monastic withdrawal). Also the connective 'yet' misrepresents the sequence; it should express 'then withdraw.'

issues.span: to hold and fill it is not as good as to let it be
issues.advice: 持而盈之不如其已 means 'to hold and overfill it is not as good as stopping/desisting.' 'To let it be' is vague; 'to stop' or 'to desist' better conveys 已.

issues.span: the way of heaven
issues.advice: 天之道 is conventionally rendered 'the Way of Heaven' (capitalized) in Daoist (Daodejing) translation; lowercase 'way' loses the technical term 道.

issues.span: success in achievement and attainment, then one withdraws

issues.span: to hold and overfill it is not as good as to stop it

issues.span: arrogance brings calamity upon oneself; wealth and honor accompanied by arrogance bring calamity upon oneself
issues.advice: The source has a single clause 富貴而驕自遺其咎 ('wealth and honor together with arrogance bring calamity upon oneself'). issues.span: rather than sharpening it, one cannot preserve it for long

issues.advice: 'stop it' is awkward for 已 (to cease/desist); consider 'it is better to stop/cease' without the object, or 'better to leave it be' to read more naturally.

For it is precisely because they are unrecognizable that they are strengthened and their demeanor is calm and easy. Like a person wading through a river in winter, they seem to fear their four neighbors; like a guest, they are open and transparent. Like ice, they are clear and unobtrusive, yet they are still. payload.translation: Celui qui sait bien faire le sage est subtil, mystérieux, profond et inconnu. C'est parce qu'il est inconnu qu'il est créé avec une grande facilité, une grande sérénité, comme si l'on traversait une rivière en hiver, comme si l'on craignait les quatre voisins, comme si l'on était un étranger, comme si l'eau se dissolvait, comme si l'on se préparait à la fonte de la glace, comme si l'on était un homme brut, comme si l'on était dans une vallée, comme si l'on était dans une masse turbulente. Qui peut rendre la turbidité calme ? Qui peut la faire s'adoucir ? Qui peut la faire s'apaiser ? Qui peut la faire s'arrêter ? Qui peut la faire s'arrêter ? Qui peut la faire s'arrêter ? Qui peut la faire s'arrêter ? Qui peut la faire s'arrêter ? C'est celui qui ne veut pas être plein qu'il peut être épuisé, qu'il peut être renouvelé, qu'il peut être créé.

issues.span: Celui qui sait bien faire le sage
issues.advice: The source 古之善為士者 means 'those in antiquity who were skilled at being a (true) officer/master' — not 'he who knows how to make the sage'. Render as 'Ceux d'autrefois qui excellaient comme maîtres/officiers'.

issues.span: 故彊為之容
issues.advice: 彊為之容 means 'one is forced to describe/characterize them' (reluctant description), not 'il est créé avec une grande facilité'. Translate as 'on est contraint de les décrire'.

issues.span: 豫若冬涉川猶若畏四鄰
issues.advice: These are similes describing the master's cautious bearing: 'hésitant comme celui qui traverse un fleuve en hiver, circonspect comme celui qui craint les quatre voisins'. The translation splits them into separate 'comme si' clauses losing the subject.

issues.span: 渙若冰將釋
issues.advice: 渙若冰將釋 = 'se dissolvant comme la glace sur le point de fondre'. The translation renders 'comme si l'eau se dissolvait, comme si l'on se préparait à la fonte de la glace', duplicating and mistaking 渙.

issues.span: 敦兮其若樸曠兮其若谷渾兮其若濁
issues.advice: These describe the master: 'simple comme le bois brut, vaste comme la vallée, uni/mêlé comme l'eau trouble'. The translation's 'comme si l'on était un homme brut... dans une vallée... dans une masse turbulente' distorts the imagery.

issues.span: 孰能濁以靜之徐清孰能安以乆動之徐生
issues.advice: This is a parallel couplet: 'Qui sait, dans le trouble, par le calme, l'éclaircir peu à peu ? Qui sait, dans le repos, par le mouvement durable, faire naître peu à peu ?' The translation collapses it into repeated 'Qui peut la faire s'adoucir/s'apaiser/s'arrêter' and omits 徐生.

issues.span: 保此道者不欲盈夫惟不盈故能弊不新成
issues.advice: Means 'Celui qui garde cette Voie ne désire pas la plénitude; c'est justement parce qu'il n'est pas plein qu'il peut être usé sans avoir à se renouveler/refaire'. The translation's 'épuisé, renouvelé, créé' misreads 弊不新成.

issues.span: 儼兮として客の若く、渙兮として冰の將に釋けんとする
issues.advice: The mixed classical/archaic constructions ('兮として', '客の若く') are awkward in Japanese; render the 兮-phrases with consistent classical-Japanese style (e.g. '儼兮として客の若し') rather than blending 兮 with modern particles inconsistently.

issues.span: 孰能濁以静之？徐清。孰能安以久動之？徐生。
issues.advice: The source is rhetorical: 'who can, being turbid, quiet it and gradually clarify? who can, being at rest, long move it and gradually generate?' The translation splits into question + fragment, losing the 'gradually' connection and the rhetorical unity; render each as a single rhetorical clause with 徐 (gradually) modifying the verb.

issues.span: 弊不新成
issues.advice: '弊不新成' is a textual crux often read as '能弊而新成' or '蔽不新成'; the translation keeps '弊不新成' literally without noting the difficulty. At minimum render it consistently with the received reading (e.g. '弊れて新たに成らず' vs '蔽れて新たに成る'); flag the ambiguity rather than silently literalizing.

payload.translation: 古に賢く士たる者は微妙玄通深不可知なり。未知にして強いて之が容を為す。識るべからざるが故に強いて之が容を為す。夫惟不可識故彊為之容豫、如冬涉川、猶如畏四鄰、儼兮として客の若し、渙兮として氷の将に釋けんとする。敦兮其若樸、曠兮其若谷、渾兮其若濁。孰能濁以静之？徐清。孰能安以久動之？徐生。保此道者不欲盈。夫惟不盈故能弊不新成。

issues.span: 未知にして強いて之が容を為す。識るべからざるが故に強いて之が容を為す。
issues.advice: The source has a single clause '夫惟不可識故彊為之容' (only because it cannot be known, one forcibly describes its appearance). The translation duplicates it into two sentences and adds an extra '未知にして強いて之が容を為す' not present in the source; remove the redundant first sentence.

issues.span: 彊為之容豫
issues.advice: '豫' belongs with the following simile (豫兮若冬涉川 = hesitant, as if crossing a river in winter), not attached to '容'. The translation leaves '容豫' fused and drops the '兮' particle; separate '豫' as the start of the next clause.

issues.span: 孰能濁以静之？徐清。孰能安以久動之？徐生。
issues.advice: The rhetorical questions are rendered as bare fragments ('徐清', '徐生') that read as disconnected statements. Render the full sense: 'who can, being turbid, quiet it so it gradually clears? who can, being at rest, long move it so it gradually lives?'

issues.span: 賢く士たる者
issues.advice: '善為士者' means 'those who were good at being a 士 (master/adept)', not 'wise and serving as a 士'. '賢く' adds a sense not in the source; render as '古の善く士たる者' or similar.

issues.span: 儼兮として客の若し、渙兮として氷の将に釋けんとする。
issues.advice: Inconsistent handling of the '兮' rhythm: some clauses keep '兮として' while '敦兮其若樸、曠兮其若谷、渾兮其若濁' are left untranslated as raw source text. Translate these uniformly (e.g., '敦兮として樸の若く、曠兮として谷の若く、渾兮として濁の若し').

issues.span: 敦兮其若樸、曠兮其若谷、渾兮其若濁。
issues.advice: These clauses are left in the source language rather than translated into Japanese; render them.

issues.span: 夫惟不盈故能弊不新成。
issues.advice: Left untranslated; render the sense 'only because he does not overflow, he can be worn/old without needing to be newly completed'.

payload.translation: I am writing a biography of Ah Q, and it has already been going on for more than two years. Yet, while I am in the process of writing it, I am constantly recalling it. This shows that I am not a man of "establishing words." For an immortal pen must be used to immortalize a man, so that men write to immortalize others, and others write to immortalize men. Ultimately, it is unclear who is immortalizing whom, until it finally resolves to immortalizing Ah Q, as if there is a ghost in my thoughts.

issues.span: it has already been going on for more than two years
issues.advice: The source says 已经不止一两年了 ('more than a year or two'), not 'more than two years'; render the indefinite duration accurately.

issues.span: I am constantly recalling it
issues.advice: 往回想 means 'to think back / reconsider / have second thoughts,' not 'recall it'; the sense is hesitation or reflection, not memory retrieval.

issues.span: so that men write to immortalize others, and others write to immortalize men
issues.advice: The source 人以文传，文以人传 means 'the man is transmitted/immortalized through his writing, and the writing through the man'—the subject is the person and the text, not 'men' and 'others'; revise to reflect 人 (the person) and 文 (the writing).

issues.span: establishing words
issues.advice: 『立言』 is a classical Confucian concept (establishing words/leaving a lasting saying as one of the three immortalities); consider a more established rendering such as 'establishing words' with awareness of the allusion, or 'leaving words for posterity,' to preserve the cultural reference.

issues.span: as if there is a ghost in my thoughts
issues.advice: 思想里有鬼似的 conveys 'as if a ghost were in my mind'—the sense of being haunted/obsessed; 'in my thoughts' is acceptable but 'in my mind' better captures the idiom.

issues.span: Yet, while I am in the process of writing it, I am constantly thinking back to it.
issues.advice: The source '一面要做，一面又往回想' means 'while wanting to write, I keep holding back / having second thoughts' — a reluctance or hesitation, not 'thinking back to it' (which suggests recalling the work). Render the sense of wavering/hesitation.

issues.span: I am writing a biography of Ah Q, and it has already been underway for more than a year or two.
issues.advice: '我要给阿Q做正传，已经不止一两年了' means the intention/desire to write has persisted for more than a year or two, not that the writing has been underway. Adjust to convey the long-standing intention.

issues.span: For an immortal pen must be used to immortalize a man, so that the man is transmitted through his writing, and the writing through the man.
issues.advice: The source '从来不朽之笔，须传不朽之人' means an imperishable pen must transmit an imperishable man — the pen transmits the man, not 'immortalize.' Keep the 'transmit (传)' wording consistent with the following '人以文传，文以人传.'

issues.span: until it finally resolves to immortalizing Ah Q
issues.advice: '而终于归结到传阿Q' means 'and in the end it comes down to writing a biography of Ah Q' — '传' here is 'write a biography,' not 'immortalize.' Also 'until' misrepresents the connective; use 'and finally.'

payload.translation: I have long desired to write a biography of Ah Q, but I am not yet finished. While I am still writing it, I constantly think back to it. This shows that I am not a man of "establishing words." For an imperishable pen must transmit an imperishable man, so that the man is transmitted through his writing, and the writing through the man. Ultimately, it is unclear who is transmitting whom, until it finally comes down to writing a biography of Ah Q, as if there is a ghost in my mind.

issues.span: I have long desired to write a biography of Ah Q, but I am not yet finished.
issues.advice: The source says '已经不止一两年了' (it has been more than a year or two), not that the writing is unfinished. Render as something like 'It has been more than a year or two since I wanted to write a biography of Ah Q.'

issues.span: While I am still writing it, I constantly think back to it.
issues.advice: The source '一面要做，一面又往回想' means 'while wanting to do it, I keep turning it over in my mind / having second thoughts,' not 'while writing it, I think back to it.'

issues.span: so that the man is transmitted through his writing, and the writing through the man
issues.advice: The source '于是人以文传，文以人传' is a set parallel: 'thus the man is transmitted by his writing, and the writing by the man.' The current phrasing reverses the order and weakens the aphoristic parallel; keep the original order and parallel structure.

issues.span: a man of "establishing words"
issues.advice: '立言' is a classical Confucian term (one of the 'three immortalities': 立德, 立功, 立言). A literal gloss 'establishing words' is opaque; consider 'a man who establishes words (li yan)' or 'one who achieves immortality through words,' preserving the allusion.

issues.span: as if there is a ghost in my mind
issues.advice: The source '仿佛思想里有鬼似的' is idiomatic: 'as if a ghost were haunting my thoughts.' The current rendering is acceptable but flat; consider 'as if something were haunting my mind.'

payload.translation: Aq is not only his name and place of origin somewhat obscure; even his former deeds are vague. For the people of Wuzhuang, as long as he helps them, they treat him as a joke, and never pay attention to his deeds. Aq himself does not say so, but when he argues with others, he occasionally squints his eyes and says: "We were once much more prosperous than you! What are you?"

issues.span: as long as he helps them, they treat him as a joke
issues.advice: The source 只要他帮忙，只拿他玩笑 means they only want him for help and only make fun of him; the causal 'as long as' misrepresents the parallel 只要…只… structure. Render as two coordinated clauses: 'they only wanted his help and only made fun of him.'

issues.span: Aq himself does not say so
issues.advice: 源文 '而阿Q自己也不说' means Aq himself also did not speak of it (his 行状), not 'does not say so' referring to the villagers' behavior. Clarify the referent: 'Nor did Aq himself speak of it.'

issues.span: squints his eyes
issues.advice: 瞪着眼睛 means to glare/open his eyes wide, not squint. Use 'glare' or 'open his eyes wide.'

issues.span: Wuzhuang
issues.advice: 未庄 is a place name; a consistent romanization such as 'Weizhuang' (or the established rendering in the edition) should be used rather than an ad hoc spelling.

issues.span: deeds
issues.advice: 『行状』 is in quotation marks in the source, signaling an ironic/archaic term for one's life record or biography. Consider 'life story' or 'record' with quotation marks to preserve the ironic tone.

issues.span: Aq is not only his name and place of origin somewhat obscure
issues.advice: The opening is grammatically awkward; restructure as 'Not only were Aq's name and place of origin somewhat obscure...' to match the 不独…连…也 construction.

issues.span: We were once much more prosperous than you! What are you?
issues.advice: The self-aggrandizing '我们先前——比你阔的多啦！你算是什么东西！' carries a mocking, dismissive tone; 'What are you?' is flat. Consider 'Who do you think you are!' to convey the contempt.

payload.translation: Aq's name and place of origin were not only obscure; even his former deeds were vague. issues.span: We were once much more prosperous than you!
issues.advice: The source '我们先前——比你阔的多啦' uses '阔' (rich/grand), and the dash indicates a pause; 'prosperous' is acceptable but 'much richer' or 'far grander' may better capture the colloquial boast and the emphatic pause.
